analysis.title: When the chips are down
key_insights: US October CPI printed 0.4% m/m headline vs 0.3% expected, core 0.3% m/m, a tenth above expectations, taking core to around 2.7% y/y. The report calls the breadth of the upside surprise undeniable.

Fed's Waller signalled openness to a 50bp hike at the next FOMC. Short-dated US rate contracts price 82bps of hikes out to October 2027. BlueBay thinks a 50bp hike in December is highly unlikely, and expects consecutive 25bp hikes in December and January, with the path after that dependent on energy prices.
BlueBay stays flat US duration but sees the US front end in overshoot territory and starting to look attractive.

The debate is whether the CPI surprise reflects second-round effects from economic strength and the Q3 energy surge (Waller's view) or whether the focus should be forward-looking, with energy prices now meaningfully lower and favourable base effects from early 2027.

BlueBay sees a lower chance of renewed US/Israel-Iran escalation. The Israeli opposition (Gadi Eisenkot) is moving to form a government and oust Netanyahu, and the scale of the Democratic midterm sweep reduces the probability that Trump returns to a kinetic war.

Europe: yields moved modestly higher in sympathy with the US, and BlueBay expects European rates to keep outperforming US rates. With escalation less likely, energy prices should resume falling, which helps European fixed income and risk disproportionately. BlueBay is modestly long outright duration in France, Italy and Romania.

UK: the BoE watchers conference reinforced the tightening message, with headline inflation set to rise into Q1 2027. BlueBay expects one or two more BoE hikes in the coming months, and sees gilts as attractive cross-region as the 'gilt premium' erodes.

Equities sold off hard after the midterms, especially AI-related sectors, then recovered this week. Semis regained most of the drawdown on reassuring CoreWeave results and funding concerns have subsided for now.

Credit is trading better after a poor October. Positioning has cleaned up, valuations are attracting dip buyers, and new issues were well received. BlueBay's investment teams are tentatively adding credit exposure.
FX: BlueBay moved to a more negative USD stance last week after the midterms, but hawkish Fed commentary complicates the path to a weaker dollar, so it trimmed conviction in the trade.

Nvidia: the report states that Jensen Huang resigned following a scandal involving reports of espionage, wiping more than $1 trillion from Nvidia's market capitalisation. The report says it can only speculate on long-term consequences. This claim comes from a single asset manager note and should be verified against primary news sources before it is used.
